paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this one. Jeremiah is locked in the courtyard of the guard, Babylon's army is outside the walls, and the word he's been preaching says the city will be captured (Jeremiah 32:2-3). Then his cousin Hanamel walks in, just as the LORD said he would, and Jeremiah says, "Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD." (Jeremiah 32:8) That's the first lesson: when what God said comes true right in front of you, even in a small moment, it's one more reason to trust Him.

Now look at what Jeremiah DOES with that trust. He doesn't just nod and say "amen." He weighs out the silver, signs the deed, calls the witnesses and hands it all to Baruch in front of everybody (Jeremiah 32:9-12). Then the LORD of Hosts tells him to put the deeds in a clay jar "to preserve them for a long time" (Jeremiah 32:14). I think that jar says it loud: believing God's word means you act like it's true, even when everything around you says otherwise.

And the promise sitting under all of it is one short line: "Houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land." (Jeremiah 32:15) So here's your big idea, baker. God's word is not just something to hear, it's something to stand on, and He keeps what He says. Don't untie that apron yet, though, because this story isn't done.
